input_signals.name: Intangible-Amplified Accrual Reversal
input_signals.expression: MUL(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(intan, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The accrual anomaly is stronger where balance-sheet intangibles are large, because intangible-heavy balance sheets give managers more discretion (capitalization, amortization, impairment timing) and give investors less verifiable information to discipline accrual-driven earnings.
input_signals.reasoning: This scales the (sign-flipped) accrual measure by the firm's rank of intangible intensity, so the signal is near zero for tangible firms and maximally negative/positive for intangible-intensive firms with extreme accruals. It is a conditional amplification, not a level effect of either theme alone.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( intan, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation-Scaled Accrual Reliability
input_signals.expression: NEG(MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1), ZSCORE(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accrual volatility proxies for the unverifiability of reported earnings, and this unreliability is priced most severely where fundamentals are already opaque; R&D-intensive firms with stable, reliable accruals are systematically undervalued relative to R&D-intensive firms whose accruals swing unpredictably.
input_signals.reasoning: The internal inconsistency is fixed by cross-sectionally centering the volatility term, so the product is genuinely two-sided: R&D-intensive firms with below-average accrual volatility take large positive values (long leg), R&D-intensive firms with erratic accruals take large negative values (short leg), and low-R&D firms are neutralized near zero regardless of their volatility. The signal is a second-moment interaction with no first-moment accrual or R&D level effect embedded in it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: neg( mul( winsor( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 1 ), zscore( winsor( vol( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 5 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Unamortized Intangible Overhang
input_signals.expression: MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dp, at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: When a large fraction of the asset base is booked intangibles but the firm records unusually low depreciation and amortization, the non-cash charge that should be flowing through earnings is being deferred, leaving stale intangible carrying values and overstated earnings that are subsequently corrected through impairments and low returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the rank-difference-of-two-anomalies construction entirely and instead builds an interaction inside the accounting identity: depreciation and amortization is the largest non-cash accrual, and its cross-sectional shortfall is economically meaningless for asset-light firms but diagnostic precisely where the balance sheet is intangible-heavy. Firms with no booked intangibles receive weight zero, so the sort is driven by the accrual-charge intensity of intangible-heavy firms rather than by intangible intensity or D&A intensity separately.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ), neg( zscore( winsor( ratio( dp, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Industry-Neutral Amortization Shortfall
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dp, at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-heavy firms that record abnormally low depreciation and amortization relative to industry peers are deferring the non-cash charge that should flow through earnings, leaving stale carrying values and overstated profits that are later corrected through impairment.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-0 version of this idea produced the strongest FMB t-stat in the batch (−3.45) but almost no FF5 alpha, and the likely reason is that a raw cross-sectional z-score of D&A intensity sorts primarily on industry capital structure, so the extreme deciles were industry portfolios that FF5 partially spans. Industry-neutralizing only the D&A leg keeps the within-industry accrual discretion signal while removing the sector tilt that was diluting the long-short spread.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ), 1 ), neg( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( dp, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Retrenchment With Accrual Support
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 1)), 0), WINSOR(RATIO(NEG(DELTA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 1)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Managers who are propping up reported earnings use two levers jointly: cutting discretionary intangible spending (real activities manipulation) and stretching accruals (accounting manipulation); firms that cut R&D while simultaneously accumulating accruals are borrowing earnings from the future twice over and subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the normalization-variant path entirely and tests a different economic mechanism — the substitution between real and accrual earnings management — which no archived signal addresses. The hurdle structure avoids the quadrant ambiguity of a double-centered product: only R&D cutters receive positive weight, so the sort is on accrual aggressiveness *within* the retrenching population, with R&D increasers and non-R&D firms neutral at zero rather than mixed into the extreme legs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( indicator( neg( delta( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 1 ) ), 0 ), winsor( ratio( neg( delta( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 1 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Goodwill Overhang With Cash Deterioration
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 1), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(oancf, 1), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Goodwill is tested for impairment against the cash-generating ability of the acquired units, so a decline in operating cash flow is a leading indicator of write-downs only for firms carrying a large acquired-intangible balance; for asset-light or organically grown firms the same cash-flow decline carries no impairment implication.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike the flagged deflator ablation, neither leg predicts returns in the direction claimed on its own — goodwill intensity is a weak stand-alone signal and one-year cash-flow change is noisy — but their product identifies a specific, dated accounting event (pending impairment of stale acquired intangibles). It also uses a cash-flow *change* rather than the ib−oancf accrual wedge, so it is not mechanically contaminated by the D&A and impairment charges that muddied the gen-0 goodwill signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ), 1 ), neg( zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( oancf, 1 ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Weakest Link Clean Innovation
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Mispricing of intangible-intensive firms requires two conditions simultaneously — earnings must be depressed by expensed investment *and* the residual earnings must be cash-validated; a firm satisfying only one condition is either an ordinary clean-accrual firm or an innovator whose reported profits are propped up by accruals, and neither is undervalued.
input_signals.reasoning: MIN of two uniform ranks is explicitly not a linear blend: a firm in the top decile of R&D but the bottom decile of accrual cleanliness scores at the bottom of this signal, whereas SUMRANK or any weighted sum would place it in the middle, so the long leg contains only firms satisfying both conditions and the two legs cannot substitute for one another. The functional form also preserves broad continuous support — the property that separated the archive's one strong alpha from the six near-degenerate weight-times-z-score conditionals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Realized Turnover On Knowledge Capital
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms are valued off revenue, but revenue that is absorbed into receivables and inventory is not yet economic revenue, and the capital base against which that revenue should be judged includes the unbooked knowledge stock; cash-realized revenue per dollar of true (tangible plus knowledge) capital identifies firms whose commercial productivity is understated on both counts.
input_signals.reasoning: This drops the ambiguous CFO-minus-earnings adjustment entirely: the accrual theme enters through the deduction of non-cash current asset growth from the revenue line, and the intangible theme through the capitalized R&D denominator, so the two corrections act on different parts of a single turnover ratio rather than being summed. Unlike the flagged version, no term reduces to a published profitability or financing-need anomaly, and the construct is continuous with support across the entire cross-section.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( sub( revt, delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ) ), add( at, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Stale Intangible Book Versus Cash Trend
input_signals.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(intan, at), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Impairment is triggered when the carrying value of intangibles can no longer be supported by the cash flows of the units that hold them, so a firm whose intangible book share is at a five-year high precisely when its cash generation is at a five-year low is carrying an unwritten-down asset and faces a forced accrual charge ahead.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the funding-gap construct, which the critic correctly read as −oancf/at plus an investment term, with a within-firm divergence that has no cross-sectional level component at all, so it cannot proxy for cash profitability or external financing need. Intangibles are deliberately not zero-filled here because the impairment mechanism is undefined for firms carrying no intangible assets, and a constant-zero series would make the time-series rank meaningless.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ts_rank( ratio( intan, at ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: Balance-Sheet Accrual Innovation Conjunction
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), ADD(DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1), dp)), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The interaction between expensed intangible investment and accrual quality should hold under any correct measurement of accruals; defining accruals from balance-sheet changes rather than the cash-flow statement tests the mechanism on a much longer and broader sample, where the intangible expensing distortion was equally present but far less researched.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal is capped near 8–14% coverage because it requires oancf, which restricts the sample to the post-1988 cash-flow-statement era; the balance-sheet accrual definition (change in non-cash working capital less depreciation) removes that constraint and should materially raise coverage while keeping the winning conjunctive form intact. If the alpha survives at higher coverage, the mechanism is robust rather than a feature of one sample window; if it collapses, we learn the cash-flow-statement definition of accruals is essential.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), add( delta( sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ), 1 ), dp ) ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Drag Burden With Cash Validation
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(dp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), revt)), RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: GAAP earnings understate economics when a large share of revenue is absorbed by non-cash charges and expensed innovation, but that understatement is only worth buying when the firm's cash generation confirms the underlying business is strong; drag-heavy firms with weak cash flow are simply unprofitable, while drag-heavy firms with strong cash flow are misread by investors anchoring on the earnings line.
input_signals.reasoning: The zero-crossing denominator is eliminated entirely: both legs are deflated by strictly positive bases (revenue and assets) and combined in rank space, so there is no discontinuity anywhere in the economically relevant region and no inverted-profitability sort. It also complements the accepted drag-plus-accrual-cleanliness conjunction by swapping only the validation leg — accrual composition versus cash-flow level — so the pair identifies which form of validation the understatement channel actually requires.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( add( dp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), revt ) ), rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Doubly Measured Accrual Cleanliness
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), ADD(DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1), dp)), at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-flow-statement accruals and balance-sheet accruals differ precisely because of acquisitions, divestitures and non-operating items, so a firm that looks accrual-clean under only one definition is often clean by measurement accident; requiring cleanliness under both identifies genuinely conservative reporting, and that verification matters most for R&D-intensive firms whose fundamentals cannot be checked directly.
input_signals.reasoning: The two accrual definitions produced the archive's two best conjunctions independently (fmb 2.14/α 5.1% and fmb 3.63/α 3.5%), and their disagreement is informative rather than noise, so intersecting them should purge the false positives that dilute each long leg. The nested MIN preserves the weakest-link property that has consistently outperformed additive and multiplicative aggregation in this archive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), min( rank( neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), add( delta( sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ), 1 ), dp ) ), at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Unbooked Equity Share With Clean Accruals
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: What drives intangible mispricing is not the rate of R&D spending but the share of a firm's true equity capital that never appears on the balance sheet; when that hidden share is large and reported earnings are cash-backed, book-anchored investors are valuing a fraction of the firm's real capital base.
input_signals.reasoning: Every intangible leg tested so far scales spending by assets or revenue, which conflates innovation intensity with asset-lightness; anchoring on book equity makes the leg a measure of how badly the balance sheet understates capital, which is the quantity the mispricing story actually names and which connects directly to how value investors screen. The denominator is strictly positive by construction for firms with positive book equity, avoiding the zero-crossing problem that sank two earlier ratios.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), add( ceq, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Restrained Innovator With Cash Proof
input_signals.expression: MIN(MIN(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5)))), RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The highest-alpha configuration found so far — innovative firms not stretching accruals above their own history — earns its return partly from firms whose accruals are low simply because the business is shrinking; requiring positive cash generation as a third condition removes the distress cases and leaves innovators whose conservative reporting is backed by real cash.
input_signals.reasoning: The 8.8% alpha of the two-leg version carried only t=2.24, the weakest reliability among the family's large alphas, which is the signature of a long leg contaminated by low-quality firms rather than of a weak mechanism. Adding a cash-profitability condition is a targeted purification of the long leg — it should shrink the alpha somewhat while raising ls_talpha and the FMB slope, and if it does not, we learn the distress cases were not the problem.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( min( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ts_rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 5 ) ) ) ), rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Step-Up With Clean Accruals
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: An increase in expensed research intensity mechanically depresses current earnings without any deterioration in economics, so when a firm steps up innovation while its remaining earnings stay cash-backed, the earnings decline investors observe is pure accounting; when the same earnings decline is accompanied by accrual inflation, the firm is deteriorating and disguising it.
input_signals.reasoning: The critique of the drag leg was that (dp+xrd)/revt loads on low-margin, high-depreciation industries; replacing it with the year-over-year *change* in research intensity removes every level effect — industry capital intensity, asset-lightness and firm-level R&D style all difference out — so the intangible leg is identified purely off the timing of investment. The archive has tested R&D *cuts* (in a degenerate gated product) but never the expansion side, and the change formulation avoids the constant-zero-series problem that would break a time-series rank for non-reporters, since they simply cluster at zero change in the middle of the sort.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( delta( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation With Asset-Side Accrual Restraint
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Total accruals mix a discretionary channel (receivables and inventory, where revenue recognition and shipment timing are managed) with largely mechanical components (depreciation, payables, taxes payable); for opaque R&D-intensive firms it is specifically the build-up of non-cash current assets that signals unverified revenue, so the conjunction should sharpen when the accrual leg is restricted to that channel.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a decomposition with economic content rather than a smoothing knob: it asks which component of the accrual measure carries the interaction, and it deliberately excludes depreciation, which the archive has shown separately behaves as a *positive* understatement signal for intangible firms and therefore works against the accrual leg when both are bundled into ib−oancf. Because it needs only act, che and at, it should also extend coverage beyond the cash-flow-statement-constrained ~8% that binds most of the archive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin-Based Intangible Capital With Clean Accruals
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Roughly half the market reports no R&D yet holds substantial intangible capital in brands, distribution networks, software and customer relationships, whose accounting footprint is a persistently high gross margin; these firms face the same expensing distortion as R&D firms, and when their high margins are also cash-backed rather than accrual-supported, the market underprices the durability of that margin.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the methodological ablation with a signal that repairs the archive's clearest structural weakness: every intangible leg tested so far assigns zero or bottom ranks to all non-R&D-reporting firms, so half the cross-section can never enter the long leg and coverage never exceeds ~11%. Gross margin is available for essentially the entire universe, making the intangible leg informative for both innovation-driven and brand-driven firms while leaving the proven conjunctive structure and accrual leg untouched.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Hidden Capital With Cash Validation
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(MAX(ceq, che), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Hidden knowledge capital is only valuable if the business generates cash; firms with a large unbooked capital share and strong operating cash flow are misclassified as expensive or unprofitable by book- and earnings-based screens, whereas firms with large hidden capital and weak cash flow are simply burning money on unproven research.
input_signals.reasoning: Cash validation was the leg that produced the archive's best FMB-plus-alpha balance when paired with the drag burden (fmb 2.98, α 4.1%, t 3.21), and pairing it instead with the hidden-capital leg tests whether the two validation concepts — accrual composition versus cash level — are substitutes or complements for the same intangible leg. Because the long leg requires positive cash generation, it should carry a cleaner risk profile than the accrual-only version, which is the diagnosed weakness behind the 8.8%/t=2.24 result.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), add( max( ceq, che ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ) ), rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Hidden Capital With Balance-Sheet Accruals
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), ADD(MAX(ceq, che), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), ADD(DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1), dp)), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The mispricing of hidden knowledge capital should be detectable under an accrual definition built entirely from the balance sheet, which is the measurement basis available for the widest sample and the one least contaminated by cash-flow-statement classification choices.
input_signals.reasoning: This combines the two legs with the strongest independent evidence in the archive — hidden equity share (α 5.3%, t 3.46) and balance-sheet accruals (fmb 3.63, α 3.6%, t 3.53, the best coverage of any conjunction at 0.106) — and shortens the R&D stock to three years specifically to recover the coverage that a five-year window costs. If it matches the five-year version's alpha at higher coverage, it is the better consolidated candidate for the final generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), add( max( ceq, che ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ) ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), add( delta( sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ), 1 ), dp ) ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Funded Innovation
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Research intensity separates into two economically opposite populations: firms that would be solidly profitable if they were not expensing their innovation, and firms that are unprofitable even before research spending; only the first group's weak reported earnings are an accounting artifact, and only that group should earn the intangible premium.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the depreciation-intensity leg — which the critic rightly noted has no basis for predicting positive returns and duplicated the drag ratio — with pre-research profitability, which is the direct accounting reconstruction of what earnings would look like if knowledge investment were capitalized rather than expensed. It is a genuine conjunction because neither leg works alone: R&D intensity alone mixes in cash-burning speculative research, and pre-R&D profitability alone is just a profitability sort with no intangible content.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net Hidden Capital With Pre-Research Profitability
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(intan, 0)), ADD(MAX(ceq, che), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Hidden knowledge capital is only worth what the underlying business can earn on it, and the correct profitability yardstick for an innovator is earnings before the expensed research itself; firms with large net hidden capital that would be clearly profitable absent their research spending are the population whose weak reported earnings are pure accounting.
input_signals.reasoning: Pre-research profitability was the strongest cross-sectional leg found (fmb 4.31 at coverage 0.146) while operating cash flow, its closest substitute, maximized the slope but halved the alpha, so this tests whether the accrual-reconstructed profitability validation preserves the portfolio spread that the cash-level validation destroyed. Unlike the cash version, this leg cannot simply be cash-based operating profitability in disguise, since it uses reported earnings with the research add-back rather than the cash-flow statement.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( sub( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), add( max( ceq, che ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ) ), rank( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Hidden Capital With Lean Operating Assets
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(intan, 0)), ADD(MAX(ceq, che), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), revt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accruals accumulate into a stock, so a firm carrying little receivable and inventory investment per dollar of sales has recognized revenue conservatively over many years, not just in the current one; that cumulative conservatism is the durable form of the accrual signal and should complement hidden knowledge capital better than a single year's accrual flow.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-4 asset-side *change* leg gave the archive's best slope but zero alpha (fmb 3.72, α 0.2%), which suggests the one-year flow is informative cross-sectionally but too noisy to build stable portfolios; the corresponding *stock* is a slow-moving characteristic that should sort portfolios far more persistently. It also introduces the only genuinely different accrual channel left untested here — cumulative operating-asset intensity rather than period accruals — while holding the winning intangible leg fixed.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( sub( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), add( max( ceq, che ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( act, che ), revt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Funded Innovation With Clean Books
input_signals.expression: MIN(MIN(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), ADD(DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1), dp)), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: An innovator that is profitable before its research spending and is not inflating its balance sheet with accrual-created assets is reporting weak earnings purely because of expensing; requiring all three conditions identifies the cleanest possible case of accounting-driven undervaluation.
input_signals.reasoning: Self-Funded Innovation produced the archive's highest FMB slope at by far its widest coverage (4.31 at 0.146) but only a 3.3% alpha, the pattern of a signal whose long leg still contains balance-sheet inflators; adding the balance-sheet accrual leg rather than the cash-flow one keeps coverage high while supplying the portfolio-relevant screen. If the alpha rises toward the hidden-capital family's 5–6% without sacrificing the slope or coverage, this becomes the most practical consolidated candidate for the final generations.

input_signals.hypothesis: The undervalued configuration is large self-built knowledge capital carried on a lean operating balance sheet, while the overvalued configuration is purchased intangibles carried alongside heavy receivable and inventory investment; both are cumulative states built over years, so measuring distance from the first net of proximity to the second should sort more sharply than either alone.

input_signals.hypothesis: A firm with a large invisible knowledge stock, a balance sheet uninflated by recognized soft assets, and genuine profitability before research spending is the complete case of accounting-driven undervaluation; without the profitability condition the same screen selects cash-burning research firms whose returns are volatile even when their alpha is positive.

input_signals.hypothesis: Two firms can show the same intangible-driven economics for opposite reasons: one has built pricing power itself, so its intangible capital is invisible and its margins are cash-backed; the other has bought pricing power, so its intangible capital sits on the balance sheet and its earnings lean on accruals. input_signals.hypothesis: Reporting conservatism has a stock dimension (how much recognized operating investment has accumulated on the balance sheet) and a flow dimension (whether current accruals are stretched relative to the firm's own history), and these are complementary rather than substitutable readings of the same managerial posture; combining them into one conservatism score before conjoining with hidden capital uses both without the dilution a third MIN causes.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive shows both accrual channels work — the stock leg gives the best slope and t-alpha (fmb 3.32, t 4.40) and the own-history flow leg the best Sharpe (0.606) — but every attempt to use two accrual conditions simultaneously has done so through a third MIN, which demonstrably thins the extreme deciles (Doubly Measured t 1.70, Restrained Innovator t 1.93). input_signals.hypothesis: Write-off policy is a management choice: within an industry, firms charging more depreciation and amortization per dollar of assets are extinguishing recognized book value faster, which understates current earnings and understates book capital exactly as expensed research does; a firm that is conservative on both margins — large unbooked knowledge stock and aggressive write-off of what is booked — is doubly understated.
